C-RECENTS-SERIALIZE.Name: Recents serialization: an encompassing store mutex over the recent-list read-modify-write, an unchanged-list write skip, and renderer-side serialization of every recents RMW so concurrent opens, save-all fan-outs and parallel folder additions all land on disk
C-RECENTS-SERIALIZE.Summary: The recents history loses entries under concurrency and rewrites the store for nothing, in three linked places. (1) The backend builds the recent list with a read-modify-write that releases the store mutex between the read and the write: two overlapping mt_recent_add commands read the same base list and the last store erases the other's insert — a lost recent entry with no error anywhere. (2) The renderer fans the race out: every save and every open fires a fire-and-forget ipcRecent.add (save-all and reopen-all produce a burst of concurrent adds straight into the backend race), and folder additions run their own unserialized read-modify-write in the renderer over the recentFolders key, so two parallel folder additions lose one folder from the five-slot history. (3) Adding a path that is already at the head of the list computes an identical list yet still persists it — a full atomic rewrite of preferences.json and a new on-disk generation per no-op. This change closes all three: an encompassing single-mutex-acquisition update on the prefs store (the set_many discipline) covering load→modify→save for the recents list, pinned by two concurrent adds from two threads against a from_path store with both paths on disk; an exact-equality write skip so an unchanged list never persists again (no new generation, no BLOCK_PERSISTED marker path, the remove-absent skip's own precedent); and chained-promise serialization queues — the filePositionStore mutation-queue shape — on ipcRecent.add in the facade and on the recentFolders RMW in the project store, with the fire-and-forget call sites byte-identical. Failing-first pins at both layers; no new user-facing strings.

Problem.Description: (1) The backend RMW has no encompassing lock (high — silent data loss). recent_add_inner (src-tauri/src/m017_recent.rs:81-90) runs load(prefs) → retain/insert/truncate → store(prefs, &current); load reads through PrefsState::get (src-tauri/src/m005_prefs.rs:312-318) which takes the store mutex, clones and RELEASES it, and store writes through PrefsState::set (:320-324) which takes the mutex again for insert+save. The two acquisitions bracket an unlocked window: two mt_recent_add commands (async commands on Tauri's pool — concurrency is real, not hypothetical) can both read the same base list and the second store persists a list without the first insert. Nothing surfaces the loss: both commands return Ok, the [Recent][add][BLOCK_RECENT_UPDATED] marker prints for both. The one-acquisition discipline that closes exactly this shape already exists one module over — PrefsState::set_many (m005_prefs.rs:332-338, «the store mutex is taken exactly once … save() runs exactly once», the C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY transaction) — but the recents path does not use it. The module's 18 inline tests (m017_recent.rs:168-391, tempfile fresh_prefs :174-179 — the module canon) cover none of this: no concurrency test, no unchanged-skip test. (2) The renderer feeds the race and runs its own (fe-comms F-015). Every save emits a fire-and-forget add — onSaved runs void ipcRecent.add(tab.pathname).catch(() => {}) (src/renderer/src/store/editor.js:513) — and every open emits another (editor.js:1934-1937, ipcRecent.add(pathname).catch(() => {})); save-all and reopen-all therefore burst N concurrent mt_recent_add invocations straight into defect (1), where all but the last writer's view is erased. Separately, folder additions never touch m017 at all: ADD_PROJECT pushes the folder through _pushRecentFolder (src/renderer/src/store/project.js:109-118), which is its own unserialized read-modify-write over the recentFolders key in the renderer — await ipcPrefs.get(RECENT_FOLDERS_KEY) → filter/unshift/cap to MAX_RECENT_FOLDERS = 5 (:106) → await ipcPrefs.set — reachable from ADD_PROJECT (:349) and racing the same way: two parallel folder additions each read the same base and the second set drops the first folder from the history. The serializedMutation precedent that fixes exactly this shape exists in the sibling util: filePositionStore's one queue for every read→transform→write of its prefs key (START_BLOCK_POSITION_MUTEX, src/renderer/src/util/filePositionStore.js:202-217, «without serialization each save read the same base store and the last write won»), with callers unchanged — the facade/store owns the discipline, not the call sites. (3) Unchanged lists are persisted anyway (db F-007). recent_add_inner always calls store() even when the computed list is identical to the loaded one — the everyday case of re-saving the file already at the head: retain removes the path, insert puts it back at index 0, the vec compares equal — and store() escalates to PrefsState::set → save_with_rename (m005_prefs.rs:195-216): a full serialize of the whole preferences.json, tmp file, fsync, rename, and the [Prefs][save][BLOCK_PERSISTED bytes=… keys=…] marker (:210-214) — a brand-new on-disk generation for a no-op, on every save of the current document. The module already knows the skip discipline one function over: recent_remove_inner returns without any store write when the path was absent (m017_recent.rs:117-135, «No store write happens for a missing path»), and filePositionStore writes back only «when anything changed» (filePositionStore.js:286). add does not skip.

Goals.R-1: ENCOMPASSING RMW MUTEX (scout key 9): the recents list read-modify-write holds the store mutex across its entire load→modify→save span. m005_prefs.rs gains a PrefsState::update mirroring the set_many discipline verbatim — the mutex is taken exactly once, the caller's closure receives the key's current value read under the guard (never calling back into the non-reentrant Mutex), produces the next one under the same acquisition, and the test gap seam lives only in the pre-fix un-encompassed form — its call site disappears with the fix, and parking inside the closure would deadlock on the mutex rather than pass; m047_bookmarks::remember stays outside the lock, ahead of the list write, exactly as today (m017_recent.rs:98), and save() runs at most once while the lock is still held (no release between read and write); a #[cfg(test)] update_with_rename twin injects the final rename exactly as set_many_with_rename does (:360-371); recent_add_inner reaches the injection through a #[cfg(test)] variant that keeps the production skip/dedupe logic and delegates the persist to update_with_rename, so the unchanged transform pins exercise the real list path rather than a re-implemented one. recent_add_inner (m017_recent.rs:81-90) moves onto it: dedupe-by-path, promote-to-head and the MAX_RECENT_DOCS cap run inside the closure; the BLOCK_RECENT_UPDATED marker, the Ok/Err contract, the bookmark grant moment in mt_recent_add (which stays ahead of the list write) and every command signature are unchanged. The failing-first pin is the module canon's own fixture: recent_concurrent_adds_from_two_threads_both_persist — two adds from two threads against one PrefsState::from_path store, made deterministic by a #[cfg(test)] gap seam parked between the loaded read and the persist (armed only inside the pin; an encompassing implementation never reaches it, so the same test is green after the fix — recorded honestly), asserting after join that a fresh from_path reload shows BOTH paths on disk; thread scheduling never decides the outcome and no sleeps are used. The recent_ prefix keeps the pin under the V-M-017 command's cargo recent filter. On the pre-change tree the parked interleaving deterministically loses one insert, so the pin is red.
Goals.R-2: UNCHANGED-LIST WRITE SKIP (scout key 11): add stops persisting a no-op. recent_add_inner compares the computed list to the loaded one (exact element-sequence equality — the ≤10-string vec compare, no fuzzy matching) and, when identical, returns Ok WITHOUT store(): no prefs write, no tmp file, no rename, no new on-disk generation, no BLOCK_PERSISTED marker path taken, and a distinct console-only [Recent][add][BLOCK_RECENT_UNCHANGED] marker naming the skip in the module's marker convention. A changed list persists exactly as today (a path already present but NOT at head changes the order and must still persist). remove-absent's existing skip (m017_recent.rs:117-135) is the module precedent and stays byte-identical. Failing-first pin: with the rename seam injected to fail (the R-1 twin), recent_unchanged_head_add_skips_the_persist adds a path already at head and still resolves Ok — proof the persist provably never ran, since a rewrite would surface the injected failure — while recent_changed_add_still_persists_through_the_seam makes the same failing seam return Err for a genuinely new add, proving the seam really fires on real writes; the reloaded list and its order are asserted unchanged. Both pins carry the recent_ prefix for the V-M-017 cargo recent filter.
Goals.R-3: RENDERER SERIALIZATION OF RECENTS WRITES (scout key 10): every recents RMW the renderer emits runs on a chained-promise queue — the serializedStoreMutation shape (filePositionStore.js:202-217: one queue per prefs key, «chained promises preserve per-caller results while composing the writes»), owned module-locally exactly as filePositionStore owns its queue. The ipcRecent facade (src/renderer/src/ipc/runtime/recent.ts:20-22) serializes add behind one queue: each mt::recent::add invoke completes before the next begins, per-caller results keep propagating (a rejecting add fails only its own caller; the queue chain survives rejections to keep serializing), and list/clear/remove/insert wrappers stay unqueued and byte-identical. Both existing call sites — editor.js:513 (onSaved) and editor.js:1934-1937 (open path) — stay fire-and-forget and byte-identical: the facade owns the discipline, the callers do not change. The project store serializes EVERY recentFolders RMW it runs behind one shared chained-queue discipline owned at the project-store action level: _pushRecentFolder (project.js:109-118) and the SET_RECENT_FOLDERS/GET_RECENT_FOLDERS actions (project.js:650-673) that the welcome screen's removeRecentFolder and undoRemove ride (recent/index.vue:624-626/:657) all compose onto the same queue, so an ADD_PROJECT racing a folder removal loses nothing (red-first pin: racing_folder_add_and_remove_both_persist); recent/index.vue itself stays untouched — its actions dispatch into the serialized store actions. Best-effort error swallowing and the cap/dedupe transforms are preserved. Failing-first pins: tests/renderer/ipc/runtime-recent.test.ts pins parallel_adds_invoke_one_at_a_time_and_all_resolve (a controlled invoke mock holding the first call pending proves NO second mt::recent::add is issued until it resolves, then every queued add resolves — red pre-fix where invokes fire concurrently) plus per-caller rejection isolation (one rejecting add does not fail the adds queued behind it); tests/renderer/store/project-coverage.test.js (the _pushRecentFolder describe at :471-508) pins parallel_folder_additions_all_persist (two racing ADD_PROJECT calls against an accumulating fake ipcPrefs store with the first get held pending — the persisted recentFolders list contains BOTH folders; red pre-fix where the second set overwrites the first), while the existing four pins in that describe stay green.

Fix direction is binding: direction (a) is the encompassing single-mutex-acquisition update on PrefsState (the set_many discipline) — a command-level queue alone is the recorded alternative and is NOT the pin target, because the defect is the lock release between load and store inside ONE read-modify-write (the two-thread pin proves the lock-level fix; a plan may additionally queue commands but not instead of the mutex fix). Direction (b) queues are module-local per prefs key — recentDocuments in the facade, recentFolders in the project store (the filePositionStore ownership precedent; sharing one helper is a plan choice per the exported-statFileExists precedent, but per-key serialization is the contract and a global cross-key queue is not required). Direction (c) skip is exact sequence equality of the computed vs loaded list — the comparison happens before persist, the skip path writes nothing at all (no tmp, no rename, no generation), and a skipped add stays Ok. Determinism bar for the concurrency pins: the backend pin's interleaving is controlled by the #[cfg(test)] gap seam (or, if the plan records why the seam does not fit, by a bounded repetition harness with its red-first evidence recorded per run) — no timing sleeps, no statistically-flaky reds; the renderer pins are deterministic through controlled pending-first mocks and accumulating fake stores with await-quiescence.

Predecessor contracts stay green and unweakened: all 18 m017 tests (add/dedupe/cap/clear, the C-46 remove/insert pins — remove_missing_path_returns_none_and_keeps_list, remove_returns_old_index_and_persists, remove_then_insert_restores_exact_order, remove_persists_across_reloads, persistence_across_reloads), the m005 set_many/quarantine/get_many pins (get_many_returns_requested_keys_without_persisting included), the filePositionStore tri-state/cap/queue pins (file-position-store.test.js :119/:144/:178/:206/:229/:255), the recentlyClosed and session-restore suites, the four existing _pushRecentFolder pins (project-coverage.test.js:471-508) and the runtime-recent.test.ts wrapper pins — all keep passing without weakened assertions; mt_prefs_get/set/set_many/get_many/get_all semantics, the atomic save shape and the mt::user-preference broadcast are unchanged.

Honesty bar: directions a–c plan NO new user-facing strings — the skip is announced by a console-only marker, serialization is silent, and the m017 marker convention already carries count/order only (never full paths; keep it that way). The ten-locale rule (en, de, es, fr, ja, ko, pt, ru, zh-CN, zh-TW, gated by tests/renderer/i18n/locale-keys.test.js, the C-10/C-12/C-32/C-56 canon) binds only if the plan surfaces a user-visible string — in that case the keys land in all ten locales in the same bundle. Concurrency is real at the command layer: mt_recent_add is an async tauri command executing on a pooled runtime, so two in-flight mt_recent_add invocations race the unlocked window without any renderer help; the two-thread unit pin models this directly against recent_add_inner + PrefsState::from_path, the same store the command reaches through State. The pin's determinism comes from the #[cfg(test)] gap seam (park between the loaded read and the persist, armed only inside the pin); an encompassing implementation never reaches the seam, which is what makes the same test green after the fix without weakening it.

The recentFolders key is renderer-owned by design (project.js reads/writes it through ipcPrefs directly; m017 never touches it), so its serialization is renderer-side (R-3) and no backend work is scoped for it; the recentDocuments queue lives in the ipcRecent facade and the recentFolders queue lives once in the project store covering all three of its RMW writers (_pushRecentFolder and the welcome-screen remove/undo actions), so per-key single queues are sufficient — a shared helper is optional.
